lines: By the time I had finished the aftermath and filed my report via comms, it was already well into the night.
I headed to the shop where Balalaika had summoned me and pushed open the heavy door.
Beyond the door, Balalaika, seated at the counter of the classical bar, noticed me and raised her glass.
Balalaika
Right on time, Kotaro. I went ahead and started without you.
Me
Good work today. Ah, Master, I'll have a soda.
Balalaika
Heh, so earnest.
Me
I-I'm still a student, after all.
Balalaika teased me, her tone and the atmosphere she carried completely different from before.
The tension in my shoulders eased slightly, and I raised the glass she had offered.
Balalaika
Cheers.
Me
Cheers.
The glasses clinked softly at the rim, and I slowly brought mine to my lips.
The carbonation fizzed across my mouth, and I felt the tension from the afternoon slowly melting away.
Standing on the battlefield was second nature to me, but it seemed I had been more nervous than I expected.
But even as I relaxed, I knew the reason she had specifically called me wasn't just to congratulate me.
I organized my thoughts while compiling the report, calmed my mind, and then reflected on what I had experienced today.
Me
Today, Balalaika, you went to the front lines and gave specific orders, but what you really wanted to show was something else, wasn't it?
Balalaika
Yes, I'm relieved you noticed.
Balalaika nodded at my words, the ice in her glass making a small sound.
Balalaika
If a commander goes to the front and gives detailed instructions, they can adapt more flexibly, and it also boosts the morale of the subordinates.
Balalaika
Kotaro, commanding from the front lines is probably your specialty, isn't it?
Me
Yes, my unit mostly engages in combat where hand signals are visible.
So, while Balalaika's command today had many fine details, her intentions and movements were things I could predict.
Then, what Teacher Asagi wanted to teach me was...
Me
How to issue commands while making on-the-spot judgments...
Me

But to do that, every member of the unit needs to have a detailed grasp and understanding of the operation overview and their own role, and mutual trust that allows for seamless coordination is crucial...
The movements I saw at Hotel Moscow today were things I couldn't have commanded with my current level of skill.
But there will surely come a battlefield in the future where that kind of movement is required.
Hearing my muttering, Balalaika let out a small laugh.
Balalaika
Correct. It seems you could read the intentions of Asagi and me without being told.
Balalaika
It is important to increase your options beyond direct command on the front line.
Me
Yes, but the barrier to entry for putting it into practice is quite high, isn't it?
Balalaika
Of course. Especially as the number of personnel increases... And the more people there are, the more effective it becomes.
It is only natural that the difficulty of command increases as the number of people being commanded grows.
Me
So, thorough preparation in advance is key.
Balalaika
There is no such thing as preparing too much. As a commander, be aware of the responsibility you bear for the lives of your subordinates.
Me
Yes. I think I will have more opportunities to command large units in the future, so I should start by training with comrades I already know well...
Me
Also, I could review past unit operation records and run simulation drills with different personnel... Maybe I could incorporate that into the academy's training as well...!
Having seen such a wonderful example, my head began to spin with a succession of tasks and the training required to address them.
As I became more aware of the captain's responsibility toward the squad members, just as I had been told, my motivation surged.
Me
Thank you for the guidance! I will do my best to live up to the expectations of you and Teacher Asagi!
I clenched my fist without thinking and made a declaration of resolve, and Balalaika smiled faintly at me.
Balalaika
Asagi has found a good successor...
With a hint of envy, she murmured those ticklish words and downed her drink.
Balalaika
Mm... Phew.
She finished the contents of the glass and set it down slowly. Along with the sound of ice clinking in the glass, a breath escaped her lips.
Her cheeks were faintly flushed with alcohol, making her look like a completely different person from her appearance on the battlefield.
The sharp gaze and the large burn scars catch the eye first, but once that impression fades, one notices her refined features.
Seeing such a beautiful woman among the respected leaders, I couldn't help but stare in awe.
Balalaika
Hm? What's wrong? Is something on your mind?
My gaze was quickly noticed by Balalaika.
Me
Ah, um, I was just wondering what you were drinking...
I blurted that out to cover my tracks, but it wasn't a lie that I was interested in the liquor itself.
People who usually enjoy cigars or cigarettes seem to know a lot about indulgences, so I wondered what kind of alcohol she preferred.
Me
(The seniors at my place all turn into a mess when they drink...)
I remembered the chaotic state of the occasional drinking parties, but I pushed that thought to the back of my mind for now.
Balalaika
This is blended whisky.
Me
Blended...?
Balalaika
It is whisky made by blending malt whisky and grain whisky base spirits.
Balalaika
I don't know which specific malts are used, but it has a lovely sherry cask aroma.
As she said this, she slowly rolled the ice in her glass.
Accompanied by a soft clinking sound, the dull reflection of light wavered on the bar counter.
It was a picturesque scene, but something suddenly caught my attention.
Me
I thought you would prefer vodka over whisky, Balalaika.
Hearing my words, Balalaika gave a wry smile.
Balalaika
A common prejudice among Japanese people.
Balalaika
Of course, I drink vodka often, but I drink other types of alcohol too.
Balalaika
Besides, you must have seen me drinking champagne at the previous party...?
Me
Ah...
Now that she mentioned it, that was indeed the case.
A wave of embarrassment rose in me for speaking based on assumptions.
Me
I'm sorry...
Balalaika
Fufu, once you can handle your drink, I'll open a good vodka from my homeland.
Me
Yes!
I was tapped on the shoulder and nodded vigorously.
By the time we share a drink together, I should have grown as a commander beyond where I am now.
Just imagining my future self made a surge of motivation rise from the bottom of my stomach.
I thought my elation was still immature, but the joy outweighed it.
Balalaika watched me like that, but her gaze suddenly drifted off into the void.
Balalaika
I look forward to it too... Just don't die before then.
Me
Balalaika...
I wanted to laugh it off as bad luck, but I painfully understood the feeling of mourning the comrades she had lost.
And this woman had overcome the deaths of her comrades and continued to fight as a foundation.
Me
Yes, I won't die.
I voiced my determination, renewing my resolve.
Balalaika
Fufu... Ah.
Before her gentle smile, the ice in the melted glass made a sound again.
